title: Shipment, Transit and Branch Delivery Schedule for Factory Production Orders
content:
This schedule sets the logistics figures for Factory Production Orders once the units leave the plant, and the class settings on cancellation after production starts or after shipment.

## Per-class transit time

| Build class | Expected transit, factory ship date to branch delivery (business days) |
|---|---|
| Custom Size Build | 2 |
| Custom Color Build | 2 |
| Specialty Glass Build | 2 |
| Specialty Shape Build | 3 |
| Impact-Rated Build | 3 |
| Architectural Wood Build | 3 |

## Figures common to all six classes

| Item | Setting in every class |
|---|---|
| Branch inspection window after delivery | 48 hours; freight damage found inside this window is a freight damage remake |
| Ship notification | the customer is told the order is on schedule or delayed 2 business days before the current ship date |
| Installation job opened | within 1 business day after branch delivery |
| Shipment date that counts for lateness | the date the final unit of the order shipped (last unit shipped) |
| Order whose contract is cancelled after production starts | stopped and closed as cancelled (allowed: yes) |
| Cancellation of an order that has shipped | not allowed: the units stay on the order and the contract's cancellation terms carry the cost |

Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding U.S. federal holidays.

## Points of reading

- Transit is an expected figure counted in business days from the factory ship date; it is longer for the Specialty Shape, Impact-Rated and Architectural Wood Build classes.
- Because lateness counts from the last unit shipped, units shipped ahead do not change the shipment date that counts.
- Hypothetical example: a Custom Color Build order whose last unit ships on a Monday with no federal holiday that week is expected at the branch on the Wednesday, 2 business days later; a Specialty Shape Build order shipping the same Monday is expected on the Thursday.
